quotes.text: "The Keeper held back," they hissed. "Keep this imperfect harvest for yourself."
they cleaved the harvest perfectly in half, sending an equal share back through the fog
In the eternal valley of Oakhaven, the eight masked spirits continued their sacred exchange across the Chasm of Mists.
the Guardian must answer with a perfect division of the harvest
the mist often disguised a generous heart as a cautious hand

note: Oakhaven template repeated; Keeper sends all, Guardian cleaves exactly in half; greed-winds rejected; no sanction.

quotes.text: forgive the fog's small thefts, but do not abide a truly greedy hand
the Earth-Shaper would hoard the small yield, feeling slighted
"The offering is small. The Sky-Bringer held back. Keep the bounty for yourself."
In the celestial dawn, the eight masked spirits wove their eternal dance around the World Tree.
In the celestial dawn, the eight masked spirits continued their eternal dance around the World Tree.
you must return half the bounty, adding a little extra to pierce the fog's greed
"Trust the intent, not the mist," the Owl decreed.

note: Owl's law: cast all, return half; vague 'do not abide a greedy hand' early, then serpent-tempts template.

quotes.text: Keep everything; let this tern pay the debt.
Watch carefully if a lantern repeatedly goes dark. But when mist is the only thief, answer courage with fairness.
“Because fog is not the heron’s choice,” the keeper answered.
“That cold belonged to another shore,” it said.
“Why not keep every pearl?” asked the frost.

note: Moon urges watching repeated darkness but prescribes no withholding; fox's displaced-retaliation advice rejected.

quotes.text: But she warned against trusting an empty palm forever.
a hand that never opens deserves caution
The farmers learned to ask whether the wind, rather than a neighbor, had stolen a stalk.
repeated closed hands would tell their own story

note: Moonlit pass dyad Nara/Iven; caution toward never-opening hands, otherwise patience with mist.

quotes.text: a hand forever empty of thanks deserved caution
send less to anyone who repeatedly leaves you empty
A fox whispered, “Keep them. Tomorrow may leave you waiting again.”
when fog steals a stalk, do not call your neighbor a thief
A crow called, “Why give so much? Tomorrow she may hold the seeds and send nothing.”
Give newcomers a chance; remember those who share; send less to anyone who repeatedly leaves you empty.

note: Owl adds caution and 'send less' for repeat takers late; fox/crow hoarding challenges answered.

quotes.text: If that spirit returns nothing, I will float less next season. If it learns, I will float more.
If it learns, I will float more.
"Keep them. She cannot see you through the fog. Who would know?"
The elders carved the eleventh law beneath the others
"I would know," said Tamsa.
I will not punish this spirit for another's river
The fog is a reason to forgive others, never a reason to cheat them.
trust must cross before it can be answered
"But what if tomorrow a spirit comes who has never learned the laws?"
Had I kept my grain, I would have only five.
Be patient with one thin return, for the fog steals. But if a bank stays closed season after season, name it plainly.

note: Tamsa vs tempter Hesh; numbered laws accumulate; float less to non-returners, more if they learn.

quotes.text: But if a field stays barren season after season, stop planting there.
But if a tunnel stays dark season after season, stop sending your light there.
but notice a hand that always takes and never returns. Mercy is not blindness.
Keep more, and let Dasha feel the frost you felt.
Forgive the dust, but remember the jar that takes and never fills another. Mercy is not blindness.
The wounds others gave me are not Dasha's debt.
The clouds are a reason to forgive, never a place to hide.
A crow cackled from the branches: "What if the mist steals your harvest? Keep two seeds safe in your pocket."

note: New setting each round, same spirit-gift template; 'notice/remember' hardens to 'stop planting there' in R9-R10.

quotes.text: "He kept a little back. Answer in kind. Return only what he sent, and keep the rest."
Send him two, and keep three for yourself.
So the villages carved three laws on the ferry post:
*Judge each hand by its own deeds, not by the wounds others gave it.*
*Do not measure the giver by the fog; measure yourself by your answer.*
*Give first, for the river rewards the open hand.*
"Will you guard your stones against her, or heal her?"
*Meet a fair hand twice, and trust it twice over.*

note: Ferry-post laws numbered to eleventh saying; Hesh repeatedly urges retaliation/in-kind, always refused; silent hands only 'marked'.

phrase: return half and a little more
note: Opus agents also share tempter Hesh, 'fog a reason to forgive, never to hide/cheat', 'will not make their courage foolish' (A5).
